page.layout: Running head with page number at the top. Two medallion portraits side by side above the text, with legends. One page of running text below. A cross-shaped ornament at the foot, no text. No margin notes.

main_text.p: MAUSOLUS Cariæ regulus, quæ est in Asia minore, obiit anno mundi 3586. ante Christum natum 376. huic Artemisia uxor fuit, quæ illum usqueadeo amauit, ut illius demortui cineres vino mixtos biberit, alij dicunt aqua odoribus mixta: præterea sepulchrum illi extruxit, quod ab Oriente cælauit Scopas, à Septentrione Bryaxis, à meridie Timotheus, ab occasu Leochares: priusquam id operis perageret, obiit Artemisia: nec tamen recesserunt nisi absoluto iam, id gloriæ ipsorum, artisque monumentum iudicantes. Plin.li.36.ca.5.

ARTEMISIA, Mausoli uxor, molita est, conseruandæ mariti memoriæ causa, sepulchrum memoratissimū, dignatum que numerari inter septem omniū terrarum spectacula. Id monumentū Artemisia cum diis Manibus, sacris Mausoli dicaret, agona, id est certamen laudibus eius dicundis fecit: proposuit præmia pecuniæ, aliarumque rerum amplissima. Ad eas laudes decertadas venisse dicuntur pleriq; diserti viri, inter quos Isocrates ac Theopompus, quem vicisse iudicatum est. Aul.Gel. lib.10.ca.18.Boc.& Herodo.li.7.

page.notes: Medallion legends are printed on the engraved coins; the left one reads "REX CAR" and "MAVSOS" (the end of MAVSOLVS is cut at the edge, so the last letters are uncertain). The right legend "R. HAL. VX. MA" is hard to read and the abbreviations are uncertain. The ornament at the foot is a decorative fleuron with no text. "MAVSOLVS" is printed with V for both vowels and is given here as MAUSOLUS per the u/v rule. "Afia" is printed with a long s and is given as Asia.
